title: Architectural Whispers: Robust Machine Learning Models Fingerprinting via Frequency Throttling Side-Channels
problem: ML model architectures are hidden to protect intellectual property, but adversaries can fingerprint them through frequency throttling-based side-channel attacks that convert power variations into timing patterns revealing the underlying model architecture.
motivation: Protecting ML model architectures from fingerprinting attacks is essential for intellectual property security and preventing model-specific adversarial attacks.
method: The attack uses frequency throttling to convert power side-channel observations into measurable timing variations during model execution. Adversary kernels induce controlled frequency throttling while a time series ML classifier analyzes execution time patterns to identify the model architecture family. The method operates at Ring 0 privilege level and demonstrates 96% accuracy across multiple platforms.
key_novelty: Novel use of frequency throttling-induced timing side-channels to fingerprint ML model architectures by correlating execution patterns with architecture characteristics.
contributions: Novel fingerprinting attack leveraging frequency throttling as a side-channel vector to detect ML model architecture families
Achieved 96% accuracy in identifying known ML model architectures across different hardware platforms
Demonstrated Ring 0 privilege-level attack effectiveness and cross-platform applicability
Publicly available implementation enabling reproducible security research
limitations: Limitations, defenses, and practical constraints are not discussed in the provided abstract.
primary_theme: ML model fingerprinting via frequency throttling side-channels
